questions.question: Highight the major fermentation based products in food industry.
questions.solution_html:
• Fermentation plays a crucial role in the food industry by producing preserved
  • flavorful products through microbial action on sugars and other substrates.
  •  Yogurt: Lactic acid bacteria (Lactobacillus bulgaricus, Streptococcus thermophilus)
  • ferment lactose in milk, creating tangy flavor, texture, and probiotics
  •  Cheese: Bacteria, yeast, and molds ferment milk sugars and proteins over
  • weeks/months, developing complex flavors and textures (e.g., cheddar, gouda).
  •  Beer: Yeast ferments barley malt sugars into ethanol and CO₂ via alcoholic
  • fermentation, producing carbonation and alcohol content.
  •  Wine: Yeast converts grape sugars to ethanol and CO₂, with malolactic fermentation
  • by bacteria softening acidity for red/white varieties.
  •  Sauerkraut/Kimchi: Lactic acid fermentation of cabbage by Leuconostoc and
  • Lactobacillus creates sour taste, preservation, and gut-healthy probiotics.
  • ( (1 mark) each for each product )
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Give a detailed account on holoenzyme.
questions.solution_html:
• Holoenzymes represent the complete, catalytically active form of enzymes that
  • require non-protein components for function.
  •  Complete enzyme complex consisting of apoenzyme (protein part) plus
  • cofactor (inorganic ion or organic coenzyme like NAD+), enabling full
  • catalytic activity.
  •  Apoenzyme alone is inactive; cofactor binding induces proper conformation
  • and stabilizes transition states for substrate catalysis.
  •  Examples include RNA polymerase holoenzyme (with sigma factor) for
  • transcription initiation and DNA polymerase III for replication.
  •  Cofactors often derived from vitamins (e.g., FAD from riboflavin, CoA from
  • pantothenic acid) act as transient carriers of electrons, acyl groups, or
  • hydrides.
  •  Essential in metabolic pathways; dissociation into apoenzyme yields inactive
  • form, providing regulatory control.

  •  Beer: Yeast ferments barley malt sugars into ethanol and CO₂ via alcoholic
  • fermentation, producing carbonation and alcohol content.
  •  Wine: Yeast converts grape sugars to ethanol and CO₂, with malolactic fermentation
  • by bacteria softening acidity for red/white varieties.
  •  Sauerkraut/Kimchi: Lactic acid fermentation of cabbage by Leuconostoc and
  • Lactobacillus creates sour taste, preservation, and gut-healthy probiotics.
  • ( (1 mark) each for each product )

questions.question: Give a detailed account on holoenzyme.
questions.solution_html:
• Holoenzymes represent the complete, catalytically active form of enzymes that
  • require non-protein components for function.
  •  Complete enzyme complex consisting of apoenzyme (protein part) plus
  • cofactor (inorganic ion or organic coenzyme like NAD+), enabling full
  • catalytic activity.
  •  Apoenzyme alone is inactive; cofactor binding induces proper conformation
  • and stabilizes transition states for substrate catalysis.
  •  Examples include RNA polymerase holoenzyme (with sigma factor) for
  • transcription initiation and DNA polymerase III for replication.
  •  Cofactors often derived from vitamins (e.g., FAD from riboflavin, CoA from
  • pantothenic acid) act as transient carriers of electrons, acyl groups, or
  • hydrides.
  •  Essential in metabolic pathways; dissociation into apoenzyme yields inactive
  • form, providing regulatory control.
